claim_text: An advance ruling may be issued for clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as it does not amount to an amendment or replacement of the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling upon application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give reasons in writing for being unable to issue it.
An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to it.

An advance ruling covers any written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.

The application must contain the taxpayer's contact details, a complete description of the issue or transaction and its financial implications, if any, and a complete description of its impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person.

The application must also give details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions of the tax authority on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.

The relevant tax authority may request additional information from an applicant and, where necessary, shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The relevant tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or persons connected to the applicant.
The effect of a ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, and it is rendered on a set of facts before the tax authority and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction actually carried out is materially different from the one described, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, from the date the repeal or amendment takes effect, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation it is based on, from the date of the judgement unless that decision is overturned.

Interest expenditure shall not be carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.

All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the additional amount of tax, even where those facts were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the taxable person in the same year.

In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount resulting from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria.

For this purpose, profit margin is the proportion of Earnings Before Interest and Tax to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. The relevant tax authority may, for satisfactory and good cause shown, extend the time for making the objection to such reasonable time in the particular circumstances.

claim_text: An advance ruling may be issued for clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, provided it does not amount to an amendment or replacement of the law.

An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to any tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to it.
An advance ruling covers a transaction, a proposed transaction or any tax matter, and is given in writing as an opinion or decision to direct or clarify.
An application must contain the taxpayer's name, Tax ID, postal address, email address and telephone number.

An application must also contain a complete description of the issue or transaction, including its financial implications if any, and of its impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person.

An application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions of the tax authority on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, and the reasons why the ruling should be granted.

claim_text: Capital allowance is made at the rate specified in Table I for qualifying expenditure that a person incurred wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business.
Table I lists Motor Vehicle Expenditure under Class 3, at a rate of 25%.
A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
If the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.
An allowance is not made for a year unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
An allowance not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business is carried forward to a subsequent period.

note: Third Schedule 30% EBITDA limit, banking and insurance exception, five-year carry-forward.

claim_text: Where a Nigerian company or a permanent establishment of a non-resident company in Nigeria incurs interest or similar expenditure on debt issued by a connected person, the excess interest is a disallowable deduction for Chapter Two purposes.

Excess interest means total interest paid or payable to a connected person that is more than 30% of the Nigerian company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation in that accounting period.
Interest on debt employed in generating the income of a trade, business, profession or vocation is a deductible expense, subject to the provisions of the Third Schedule.
The limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company that is engaged in the business of banking or insurance.

Interest expenditure that is not wholly deducted for an assessment year is carried forward to the following assessment year or years. It is allowed against the profits, if any, of any business carried on by the company and assessable for that year, to the extent permitted under paragraph (2) of the Schedule.
Interest expenditure is not carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately after the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.

For the Schedule, debt means any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges that are deductible in computing income chargeable under the head profits and gains of business or profession.
A deduction is not allowed for any payment to a connected person that is not consistent with the Transfer Pricing Regulations issued by the Service.

claim_text: Subject to this Act, any tax law or regulation, a company that has been in business for more than 18 months must file its returns not more than six months after the end of its accounting year.
Every company must file a self-assessment return with the Service at least once a year, with or without notice from the Service, whether or not it is liable to pay tax.
A company that permanently ceases to carry on trade or business in Nigeria must file not later than six months from the date it permanently ceases.

note: Section 11(1)(b) proviso (attested statement for a small company); definition.

claim_text: Every company must file a self-assessment return with the Service in the prescribed form at least once a year, and the return must contain, among other things, the audited financial statements, tax and capital allowances computation for the year of assessment for the profit from each and every source.
Under a proviso, the return of a small company may contain a statement of accounts attested to by the taxpayer in place of audited financial statements.
A small company is defined as a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
Under that definition, any business providing professional services is not classified as a small company.

note: Section 36(1), (2), (4) and (5) (six years; deliberate misstatement at any time). Minor: the section 43(4) claim drops "the provisions of section 41" ("is not prevented" / repeat 3 "may make"); not material to the question.

claim_text: Where the relevant tax authority discovers or is of the opinion, at any time, that a taxable person liable to tax has not been assessed or has been assessed at less than ought to have been charged, it may, within six years of the assessment, assess the taxable person at the amount or additional amount that ought to have been charged.
The six-year limit does not stop the relevant tax authority from continuing a tax audit and raising an additional assessment where the tax audit began before the six-year limit expired.

Despite the time limit in subsection (1), where a taxable person makes a deliberate misstatement in connection with any tax imposed under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 or any other tax law, the relevant tax authority may at any time, and as often as necessary, assess the taxable person for the amount needed to make good any loss of tax attributable to the deliberate misstatement.

All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the amount or additional amount of tax that should have been charged, even where those facts were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the same year.

The tax authority may make an assessment or additional assessment for a year if it does not involve re-opening any issue on the same facts that was determined for that year under section 41(5) by agreement or on appeal.

claim_text: Where a business produces no assessable profit, or an assessable profit less than expected from that business, or where the true amount of the assessable profit cannot be readily ascertained, the relevant tax authority may act under the deemed profit rule.
In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount resulting from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria.

Profit margin means the proportion of EBIT to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. For persons not required to publish financial statements, it is the profit margin the relevant tax authority ascertains from financial statements of comparative companies.

note: Section 49(3) abeyance, with the duty to pay the undisputed part; 30-day rules.

claim_text: Subject to section 11 of the Act, collection of tax where the taxable person has given notice of an objection or appeal remains in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined.
The taxable person must still pay the tax that is not the subject of an objection or appeal.

When an objection or appeal is determined, the relevant tax authority serves the taxable person a notice of the tax payable as so determined, and that tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of that notice.
Where there is no objection or appeal, the relevant tax authority may proceed to enforce recovery of the tax payable in accordance with the Act.

A written notice of objection is valid only if delivered to the relevant tax authority within 30 days from the date of service of the disputed notice of assessment, and it contains the grounds of objection listed in the section; the authority may extend this time for satisfactory and good cause shown.

note: Section 56(3): 30 days, refund or set-off in the same claim (D-45 shape).

claim_text: Where a valid VAT refund request is received from a taxable person, the Service shall, not later than 30 days of receiving the request, refund the tax to the taxable person, or the amount shall be eligible for set-off against any tax liability of the taxpayer.
The request for a VAT refund is to be made to the Service in the prescribed form, not later than 12 months after the transaction giving rise to the refund, otherwise it lapses.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not utilised as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.

note: Section 192(1) to (4) restated.

claim_text: Section 192 deals with transactions between related parties, which must be at arm's length.
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall ensure that the terms and conditions of the arrangement are at arm's length.
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall report the arrangement in the form and manner prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where, in the opinion of a relevant tax authority, a company has entered into an arrangement with a related party that is not at arm's length, the authority may make necessary adjustments to bring it in line with arm's length terms as provided under the Transfer Pricing Regulations.
The relevant tax authority may make rules or regulations for the administration of section 192.
For section 192, an "arrangement" includes any agreement, understanding, scheme, financial or commercial relation, transaction or series of transactions.
For section 192, "arm's length terms and conditions" means the terms and conditions obtainable if the transaction or arrangement was between unrelated parties dealing in comparative circumstances.
Section 192 makes the tax authority's adjustment power subject to the Transfer Pricing Regulations, and it also refers to rules or regulations the relevant tax authority may make.

note: Section 66 remission power and the relevant-tax-authority definition.

claim_text: The relevant tax authority may, for any good cause shown, remit the whole or any part of a penalty or interest due under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act or any other tax law.
The relevant tax authority may also make a monthly report to the Minister or commissioner responsible for finance, giving details of the taxpayers, the circumstances and the amounts waived.
"Relevant tax authority" means the Nigeria Revenue Service, the Internal Revenue Service of a State or the Federal Capital Territory in Nigeria.

claim_text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, at 0% for a small company.
Tax on any other company is levied at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less the amount of any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance under Part I of the First Schedule.
A company includes dividend income in its profits, gross of any tax paid or deducted at source.
Dividends received by a Nigerian company by way of shares of the paying company are not included in its profits chargeable to tax under the Act.
Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, it must recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%.

This minimum tax rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

claim_text: Section 191(2) of the Nigeria Tax Act says the provisions on objections and appeals under Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 apply to a direction made under section 191.

A direction under section 191 is one the relevant tax authority may make where it considers a transaction artificial or fictitious, or a disposition not given effect to; it may disregard the transaction or make adjustments and issue an assessment or additional assessment.
